Here is the outcome list for staging the project. I took the candidates from the spec's rulings (§3), with §4 and §7 filling in what each one means. Nothing is ranked yet; that is your call.

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A canonical filing-index Parquet catalog for a chosen range of archived quarters | R1, R3 | Requests are trivial: about 4 per year of range (one per quarter plus listings), so a 30-year range is about 120 files, under a minute at 3 req/s. Bytes and parse time dominate. **Not estimated**: I haven't looked up `master.idx` sizes, and the first stage measures it |
| O2 | New daily indexes are added to the catalog, with catch-up after missed runs, including across quarter boundaries | R2 | About 250 small files per year. Negligible request load. Partner time goes to choosing the handoff date |
| O3 | A parser change can be replayed from the stored original bytes without re-downloading | R6 | Storage roughly equals the raw bytes of O1 and O2, kept indefinitely. Size follows from O1's measurement |
| O4 | A weekly re-read of every quarterly index records additions and field changes | R7 | One full re-download per run, the same volume as O1, so weekly volume equals the full baseline. Measured by O1 |
| O5 | Removed filings leave the active catalog only after you approve the exact source hash | R10 | Your time per gated quarter. Frequency is unknown until reconciliation runs on real data |
| O6 | Readers always get a complete quarter through one active pointer, never partial files | R9 | No material cost |
| O7 | All SEC traffic shares one request budget, however many workers run | R8 | No material compute. It caps throughput at 3 req/s (SEC ceiling is 10) |
| O8 | Everything runs on schedule in Azure, with alerts, runbooks and rollback exercised | R4, §4.7–4.9, §7 Phase 2 | **Not estimable without running**: ADF, Container Apps, ADLS and Log Analytics charges depend on the sizes O1 measures. The spec itself defers cost and freshness guarantees (§2.2) |

## Tracks

- **One track, known progression.** Every outcome serves the same use, the catalog, and none stands without O1's baseline. Reconciliation, withdrawals and replay all act on a catalog that already exists. The spec's §7 phases name the progression from first stage to last. If you would rather treat the Azure deployment (O8) as its own track, say so. I didn't split it out because it answers no separate question: it is where the catalog runs.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 in a uv workspace (`.python-version`, root `pyproject.toml`).
- All ingestion code lives in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest` (spec §4.9). The other three scaffolded packages (`sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download`, `sec-edgar-index-ingest`) aren't named by the spec, and I'll leave them out of the roadmap unless you say otherwise.
- Azure platform: ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS and Table Storage (R4). The ADR is still **Proposed**, so I'm recording this as the spec's choice, pending your acceptance.
- Backfill, daily and reconciliation share one downloader, parser and publisher (R5).
- The §4.8 defaults are starting values (R11), including 3 req/s and the 5-attempt retry policy.

## Roadmap name

`specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`. The rules fix this to the spec's filename stem.

## Optional probe

I could firm up O1's cost by fetching one `full-index` quarter's `index.json` listing to read the file sizes. That is one read-only request with a User-Agent you'd supply. I'll only run it if you say yes.

---

**Please rank O1–O8, and confirm or change the single track, its kind (known progression) and the package scoping above.** Once you've answered, I'll write the stages.
